newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan swam to safety as 26 immigrants vanished.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan swam to safety as 26 immigrants vanished.

text.p: A Moroccan fisherman whose boat sank carrying 26 would-be illegal immigrants to Spain, pleaded guilty on Monday in Tangier court to charges of being responsible for their deaths.
Abdelaziz Fellah Boughaba, 27, told the court in the northern city: "It was the first time I had done something like this."
Boughaba was arrested last Monday after he told police his boat sank in the Strait of Gibraltar while trying to reach the southern Spanish coast.

His vessel, the six metre (20-ft) Moujahid, had a legal carrying capacity of six. The 26 Moroccans, from Nador district on the Mediterranean coast, had paid Boughaba 4,000 dirhams ($460) each to take them to Spain, the court heard.
According to officials, two bodies have so far been recovered near the Moroccan coast.
Boughaba told the court he was the only one with a life jacket and had managed to swim ashore.
His lawyer asked the court to free him, saying the Moroccan government was to blame for a policy of "marginalising" the country's young people so they sought to emigrate.
T impose a five year prison sentence.
A verdict is expected on Tuesday.
